sections: Design Pillars: What is Central to the Experience?

candidate.description: Hauled freight for years, now runs a dirt track in Hoon. Stubborn as a stuck diesel, with a spare tire to match. Pick up your cigarette butts or he'll pick you up.

llm_verdict.summary: The candidate has no blocking issues. The id and display_name are exact. The tagline is about 35 characters, under the 40 limit. The description is about 160 characters in three short sentences, inside the 80-220 range. It reflects both required background elements: long-haul trucking ("Hauled freight for years") and the dirt track in Hoon. The stubbornness, spare tire and cigarette-butt grudge all come from the GDD and Style Guide. It adds no invented biography, titles, moves or match mechanics. The tone is dark, irreverent and Southern, and it suits a portrait-side panel on a 960x540 screen.

final.description: Hauled freight for years, now runs a dirt track in Hoon. Stubborn as a stuck diesel, with a spare tire to match. Pick up your cigarette butts or he'll pick you up.

candidate.description: Expelled at sixteen, he found his calling in the backyard. Two football-playing big brothers made him tough as a boot. Eyeliner over eye black, and he's fresh out of patience for loudmouth rednecks.

llm_verdict.summary: No blocking issues. The id, display_name and fields are valid. The tagline is about 29 characters, within the 40 limit. The description is about 197 characters in three sentences, within 80-220. The text matches the GDD profile: expelled at sixteen, backyard wrestling, football-playing older brothers, eyeliner over eye black, and no patience for rednecks. It invents no mechanics, titles or records. The tone is fitting but a bit mild. Three minor suggestions follow.

issues.explanation: The GDD says only "college football playing older brothers" and gives no count. "Two" is a small invented specific. The text also drops "college".
issues.recommendation: Say "Football-playing older brothers" or "College-football older brothers" and leave out the number.

issues.quote: Expelled at sixteen, he found his calling in the backyard.
issues.explanation: The task asks for his trailer-park goth identity. The text implies goth only through the eyeliner and never names the trailer park or the goth look. The dark Southern humor is also mild.
issues.recommendation: Add a trailer-park or goth touch, such as a trailer-park goth reference or black lipstick, and a sharper darkly funny line.

issues.explanation: It is serviceable but generic. "Beware" reads a little mainstream rather than irreverent early-90s arcade attitude.
issues.recommendation: Make it more irreverent and specific to Duckville, for example by pairing the eyeliner with taking on the neighborhood rednecks.

final.description: Expelled at sixteen, he found his calling in the backyard. Two football-playing big brothers made him tough as a boot. Eyeliner over eye black, and he's fresh out of patience for loudmouth rednecks.

messages.text: Pick up your cigarette butts on the way out, Peaux.
Hot Potato's still hot. Tell the punks.
Back to the dirt track. I got a trailer to guard.
Eyeliner didn't even smudge. Sorry, Barry.
My brothers hit harder, Barry. Way harder.

llm_verdict.summary: No blocking issues. All 8 lines use valid ids ("barry", "peaux"), with 4 per wrestler (within the 2-4 limit). Every line is well under 90 characters and has no placeholders. Names are spelled correctly. The lines draw on GDD details: Barry's cigarette-butt grudge, dirt track, trailer and stubborn streak, and Peaux's eyeliner, brothers, expulsion at sixteen and dislike of rednecks. None of them introduces a non-KO victory condition, a move or an invented biography. The tone is dry Southern trailer-park humor, and the two characters' lines are similar in length and style.
